Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Downtime reconciliation request — Nebula platform incident Apr 19

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the incident summary earlier. Our engineering lead has reconciled our traffic logs and flagged a discrepancy for the 20:23–21:05 UTC window on Apr 19. Per our contract (Section 4.2) that should qualify for a service offset. Can you confirm the final eligible minutes and an estimated credit amount so we can close the month-end books?

From: kimberly.park@redwoodai.com <kimberly.park@redwoodai.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@nebulasolutions.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwoodai.com, evelyn.hart@redwoodai.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Downtime reconciliation request — Nebula platform incident Apr 19

Hi Alicia —

Appreciate the quick reconciliation. We're reviewing our telemetry now and I want to align on method before we publish numbers. Quick notes:

- Redwood's SLA measures per-customer available requests per 30-day window. We calculate eligible downtime based on the overlap between customer requests and region outage windows.
- Preliminary look shows a 38-minute degradation in the us-west-2 cluster that aligns with your reported window.
- We need to confirm whether Nebula had emergency failovers that generated synthetic traffic; that changes the eligible request denominator.

Can you confirm whether your team performed any cross-region reroutes during 20:15–21:15 UTC? If not, we'll proceed with the standard calculation and send an itemized workbook.

I'll loop Marcus (billing) and Evelyn (ops) to prepare the calculation and approval path.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodai.com

Attachment: sla-calculation-workbook.xlsx

---
From: Ryan Chen <ryan.chen@nebulasolutions.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwoodai.com, Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@nebulasolutions.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Downtime reconciliation request — Nebula platform incident Apr 19

Hi Kimberly,

We did an emergency failover at 20:31 UTC (manual) but traffic was redirected successfully within ~90s. We can share the failover traces; however, the window Alicia referenced still captured a significant drop in successful inference calls.

I'll attach a short span log if that helps.

Thanks,
Ryan

---
From: marcus.lin@redwoodai.com <marcus.lin@redwoodai.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@nebulasolutions.com>, kimberly.park@redwoodai.com
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwoodai.com
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Downtime reconciliation request — Nebula platform incident Apr 19

Hi Alicia,

Thanks for the additional failover context — that helps. We completed the eligibility calculation per contract and our internal playbook; summary below:

- Incident window considered: Apr 19 20:15–21:10 UTC (55 minutes)
- Overlapping customer-impact minutes (requests failing or >5x latency): 42 minutes
- Adjusted for your documented manual failover (90s), we exclude the 1.5 minutes of planned reroute
- Final eligible downtime: 40.5 minutes
- SLA entitles Nebula to a monthly uptime credit prorated on request minutes: (40.5 / (30*24*60)) * monthly subscription fee

We've computed a provisional credit of $1,212.50 against invoice INV-NEB-20270430. Please see attached workbook for line-by-line math and a downloadable credit memo draft. Next steps:

1) Please confirm acceptance of the calculation by Apr 29 EOD so we can apply the credit to your April invoice.
2) If you prefer a different application (one-time refund vs. invoice credit), let us know and we'll route to finance.

Attachments: sla-calculation-workbook.xlsx, nebula-credit-memo-draft.pdf

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Revenue Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodai.com
